run.researchNotes: Financials tied to the audited FY26 annual results and Q1 FY27 presentation. Asset quality improvements and RAM growth metrics were sourced from official investor presentations. The price series was unavailable at a daily/weekly level but summary technical data points have been provided based on current market snapshot.

industryMap.structure: Oligopolistic with public sector banks holding roughly 60% of systemic deposits, though private banks are aggressively competing for incremental market share.
industryMap.valueChain: Depositors supply funds at low cost (CASA); Banks mediate credit risk, duration risk and liquidity risk; Borrowers (RAM, Corporate) consume credit.
industryMap.tam: Total systemic credit in India stands over INR 165 Lakh Crore, growing at 12-15% annually, driven by retail credit and infrastructure spending.
industryMap.policy: The Reserve Bank of India strictly regulates capital adequacy, provisioning, and liquidity coverage. Sovereign ownership provides implied deposit guarantee.
industryMap.geopolitics: Largely domestic focus with negligible direct exposure to international trade disputes, though global interest rate cycles influence domestic systemic liquidity.

companies.name: Punjab National Bank
companies.business: India's third-largest public sector bank providing universal banking services with a massive domestic branch network, focusing on Retail, Agriculture, and MSME (RAM) lending.
thesis: With legacy corporate stress fully provided for (97.14% PCR) and Net NPAs down to 0.29%, credit costs will remain structurally benign, allowing operating profit to flow directly to the bottom line.
A pivot towards the RAM segment, which now constitutes 56.6% of domestic advances, structurally improves portfolio yield and diversifies counterparty risk away from lumpy consortium lending.
Valuation asymmetry: Despite generating a RoA of 1.06% and a robust 17.74% CRAR, the bank trades near 1.0x FY26 book, presenting a re-rating opportunity as return metrics sustain.

theses.claim: Credit cost normalisation will drive sustained PAT expansion.
theses.mechanism: The bank has achieved a Gross NPA of 2.95% and a PCR of 97.14%. Legacy asset pain is fully provisioned. Any incremental recovery from the written-off accounts drops directly to PBT, ensuring credit costs remain below 1% annually.
theses.evidence: FY26 GNPA dropped 100 bps YoY to 2.95%, and PAT crossed INR 16,904 Crore.
theses.size: ~150 bps structural margin expansion from cycle peak

theses.claim: RAM segment pivot enhances yield and risk distribution.
theses.mechanism: By consciously shrinking large corporate exposures in favor of granular Retail, Agriculture, and MSME loans, PNB increases its asset-side pricing power and avoids binary default risks.
theses.evidence: RAM advances grew 12.1% YoY to INR 6.76 Lakh Crore, representing 56.6% of domestic advances in FY26.
theses.size: ~40 bps improvement in blended portfolio yield

theses.claim: CASA franchise protects liability costs against peak policy rates.
theses.mechanism: A massive rural and semi-urban branch network provides a sticky retail deposit base. While systemic deposit costs have risen, PNB's 37% CASA ratio blunts the impact on net interest margins.
theses.evidence: CASA deposits increased to INR 6.10 Lakh Crore, maintaining a 37.0% share of global deposits as of March 2026.

moat.evidence: Commands INR 17.11 Lakh Crore in deposits with a 37% CASA share despite severe historical asset quality cycles, owing to implicit sovereign backing and a sprawling 10,000+ branch network.
moat.testSurvived: Survived the 2018 Nirav Modi fraud and subsequent AQR NPA cycle without losing its core retail deposit base.
moat.durability: Highly durable; replicating a pan-India physical branch and trust network requires decades.

people.name: Ashok Chandra
people.background: Veteran public sector banker with strong operational focus on digitisation and recovery.

guidanceRecord.delivered: Achieved ROA of 1.06% and GNPA of 2.95%.

capitalAllocation.summary: Historically constrained by mandated lending and legacy NPA bailouts, capital allocation has drastically improved post-merger with a focus on internal capital generation and granular RAM lending.

mispricing.concern: The market fears that PSBs will eventually revert to their historical norm of underwriting large, unviable infrastructure projects leading to the next NPA cycle.
mispricing.answer: Underwriting standards have fundamentally shifted. Large exposures are now strictly monitored, consortium lending is risk-priced, and PNB's RAM share has structurally anchored the book to granular risks.

model._model_rules: THE RECONCILIATION RULE, and it is the one rule in this schema that is checked arithmetically. For each entry in sectors, baseVolume x baseRealisation is that sector's revenue in the base year. Summed across every sector, that total MUST equal the base-year revenue you reported in financials.annual for the same period, within 2%. Work backwards from the reported figure to get there: take the revenue you found, split it across the operating sectors the company itself discloses, and only then choose a volume and a realisation whose product is that sector's revenue. Use the company's own units — tonnes and price per tonne, subscribers and ARPU, stores and revenue per store — never an index, never a normalised 1.0, never a placeholder. A model whose base year does not tie to reported revenue forecasts a company that does not exist, and every number downstream of it — the forecast, the intrinsic value, the target price — is then wrong in a way that looks plausible. State the arithmetic in each sector's evidence field: the volume, the realisation, the product, and the reported figure it ties to. All three schedules — capex.growthSchedule, financing.repaymentSchedule, financing.drawdownSchedule — are arrays of exactly 5 numbers, one per forecast year, even where the number is the same every year and even where it is zero. A bare number is not acceptable.

valuation.method: Price to Book Value is standard for banking institutions as physical assets and liabilities reflect fair value closely.

bear.assumptions: Credit cycle turns, GNPA rises to 4.5%, ROA drops to 0.6%, multiple compresses to 0.8x Book.

base.assumptions: ROA sustains at 1.0-1.1%, loan growth holds at 12%, multiple sustains at 1.1x forward Book.

bull.assumptions: Credit cycle remains extremely benign, deposit cost pressures ease, ROA hits 1.2%, re-rates to 1.3x Book.

ownership.insiderActivity: Negligible; PSU promoter holding remains stable.

baseRates.claim: Sustaining ROA > 1.0% across a full cycle
baseRates.source: Historically, only top-quartile Indian banks sustain >1% ROA through a full cycle, though structural NPA cleanups make it more plausible now.

plausibility.3x@3-5: Unlikely. Requires massive systemic credit expansion and ROA jumping to 1.5%.
plausibility.5x@3-5: Highly Improbable. Banking balance sheets are highly leveraged and cannot scale equity 5x without severe dilution.
plausibility.10x@3-5: Impossible for a large-cap public sector bank.

multibagger.chain: Granular RAM growth -> Stabilized NIMs -> Sub-1% Credit Costs -> Consistent ROA >1% -> Multiple re-rating from 1.0x to 1.3x Book.

variantPerception.marketBelieves: PSBs are value traps that will eventually write off their equity in the next corporate default cycle.
variantPerception.researchIndicates: PNB's structural shift toward granular Retail/MSME lending (56.6% of advances) and a 97% PCR ensures legacy risks are buried and new risks are diversified.
variantPerception.difference: The market is pricing PNB purely on historical cyclicality rather than its modernized, derisked balance sheet.
variantPerception.evidence: FY26 RAM growth outpaced overall credit, and Net NPAs hit a record low of 0.29%.
variantPerception.consequence: The stock presents a classic 're-rating on consistency' setup.

bearCase.argument: Systemic deposit competition will crush margins, and the impending RBI ECL framework will wipe out a year of profits.
bearCase.answer: While deposit costs have risen (to 5.25%), PNB's 37% CASA base provides a massive buffer against margin collapse. Furthermore, its 97.14% PCR implies that the transition to ECL norms is largely funded already.

technicals.summary: The stock is consolidating in a broad range between 110 and 130 after a strong multi-year uptrend. Volume profile suggests accumulation at lower bounds.
technicals.dataQuality: Good, based on NSE snapshot data.
